# Fix round 6 (Android phone, printers): ticket settings preview, the "Local network access is not permitted" message, class C in the printer screens, the IP keyboard

Date: 2026-11-20 (emulator clock 07:38 to 08:10). Branch `feature/theming-native`, local commits only. Device: Android phone `emulator-5556` (AVD `OBizTest`, Android 17 / API 37, 2.625 px per dp, Debug build from Metro 8097, local API). Screenshots: `<scratchpad>/pass7/android/NN-*.png` (scratchpad = `/private/tmp/claude-502/-Users-work-Ordering-ordering-app-business-theming/3f70efc6-0154-439f-b577-4c786cf37ae6/scratchpad`), every one opened. Every adb call named the device. The iPhone was **not seen by me**.

Verdicts: **fixed and seen** / **no change needed (cause found)** / **not mine (proposal)** / **not seen**.

## 1. Ticket settings' preview is cut (class B): fixed and seen

**Cause.** `PrintTicketSettings/index.tsx` showed the first `PREVIEW_LINES = 14` lines of the real ticket (46 lines with every option on): the paper ended at "Internal Number: 4", so Product options, Totals and Payments (all below the cut) never changed it. The mockup's paper (`TicketSettings.dc.html`, `SPECS.md`) is a short sample that reaches the TOTAL; the real generic ticket cannot be that short and still show the 25 detail options.

**Fix.** The phone keeps a short paper (14 lines, plus a `...` line where the ticket goes on) but it is a window onto the ticket that moves to the first line the last switch changed (the first line where the ticket text before and after the switch differ, with 3 lines of context above, clamped so the window never runs past the ticket). So every switch, the six and the 25 under "Details", changes what the paper shows, and a switch near the end (Payments, Totals) shows the TOTAL. The paper is no longer inside the scrolling list: it sits above it, so the rows can be pressed while the paper stays in view (the first version in the page's scroll put the toggles half a screen below the change). The landscape tablet is unchanged (whole paper beside the switches). No number was raised; `TicketPaper` is untouched.

Files: `src/ui/src/components/PrintTicketSettings/index.tsx`, `.../__tests__/PrintTicketSettings.test.tsx`.

**Test.** New (phone, with a 40-line ticket whose lines depend on the options): starts at the top and marks that it goes on; for each of customer, products, totals, payments the text of the paper with the switch on contains its line and with it off does not (and differs); a switch at the end reaches "Total $28.50". 15 tests in the suite pass.

**Seen on `emulator-5556`** (a saved generic printer with a made-up Bluetooth address, deleted at the end): `12` (start: top 14 lines and `...`), `13` Payments off (window moved to Size / Comment / Lemonade / Subtotal / Delivery Fee / Driver tip / Total; no "Payments" lines), `14` Totals off (no Subtotal, Delivery Fee, Driver tip; Total shown), `15` Product options off (no Size / Comment lines). All three switched back on at the end (the stored ticket options are the defaults again).

## 2. "Local network access is not permitted" on Android 17: no change needed, cause is the Debug build

**What the documentation says** (developer.android.com, read in full):
- [Local network permission](https://developer.android.com/privacy-and-security/local-network-permission): the runtime permission `ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK`, in the existing `NEARBY_DEVICES` permission group (a user who already granted another permission of that group is not asked again), is **enforced from Android 17 (API 37) for apps that target Android 17 or higher** (target SDK 37+). It covers every socket to a local address (outgoing / incoming TCP, UDP unicast / multicast / broadcast), raw sockets, mDNS, `NsdManager`, OkHttp, Cronet.
- Same page, "Split permission model": for **target SDK below 37 the app "receives an implicit permission grant for `ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK`" with `INTERNET`, and "Don't request `ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK` at runtime prior to targeting SDK 37"; "don't add `ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK` to your manifest"**. Opting in earlier (the Android 16 compat flag `RESTRICT_LOCAL_NETWORK` + `NEARBY_WIFI_DEVICES`) is deprecated. Paths for target 37+: a system picker (`NsdManager` `FLAG_SHOW_PICKER`, Output Switcher) or the declared + requested runtime permission.
- Also [Behavior changes: apps targeting Android 17](https://developer.android.com/about/versions/17/behavior-changes-17) and the [Manifest.permission reference](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/Manifest.permission) (protection level dangerous).
- This app: `targetSdkVersion` 36, `compileSdkVersion` 37 (`android/build.gradle`), `dumpsys` on the phone: `targetSdk=36`. So by the documentation **nothing is required** for it (no manifest line, no runtime request), and adding either is what the page says not to do.

**What actually produced the message** (not a guess):
1. The text is the Star SDK's: `StarIO10ErrorMessage.LocalNetworkAccessIsNotPermitted` in `node_modules/react-native-star-io10/android/src/lib/stario10.aar` (`javap` of `StarIO10ErrorMessage`, the discovery managers `stardevicediscoverymanager/e` and `rawport/j`): `if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 37 && context.checkSelfPermission("android.permission.ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK") == PERMISSION_DENIED) throw StarIO10IllegalHostDeviceStateException("Local network access is not permitted.", NetworkUnavailable)`. Not a socket error, not the Epson library.
2. Why the check says denied on this phone: the **Debug** merged manifest declares `<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK"/>` (`android/app/build/intermediates/merged_manifest/debug/...`; it comes from React Native's own `node_modules/react-native/ReactAndroid/src/debug/AndroidManifest.xml`, with the comment "apps that declare this must hold ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK to reach the dev server"; `LocalNetworkPermissionUtil.kt` asks for it at launch in debuggable builds). **The app's own `AndroidManifest.xml` and `src/debug/AndroidManifest.xml` do not declare it, and the Release variant does not** (only `debug` and `debugOptimized` of React Native do). A declared permission is no longer implicitly granted, so it has to be held; on this emulator the system dialog is dismissed at once (`result=2`), leaving `ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK: granted=false, flags=[USER_SET|USER_FIXED...]`.
3. Evidence, Star + Wi-Fi/LAN search on `emulator-5556` with Bluetooth granted (so the known Bluetooth gate, item 4, is out of the way):
   - Debug as built, permission denied: "Local network access is not permitted." (`04-lan-search-bt-granted.png`).
   - Same, `pm grant ... ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK`: the search runs and ends "No printers found" (no printer on the LAN) (`05-lan-search-all-granted.png`).
   - A Debug build with the declaration **removed** (a temporary `tools:node="remove"` line in the app manifest, built, installed on `emulator-5556` only after `pm uninstall`, then reverted and rebuilt): `dumpsys` shows no declaration and `ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK: granted=true, flags=[REVOKE_WHEN_REQUESTED]` (the documented implicit grant) from the install, Metro loaded with no permission prompt, and the same search ends "No printers found" with nothing asked (`09-lan-search-not-declared.png`). That is what a target-36 Release build is.
- A real device with a Debug build shows the permission dialog at launch (React Native asks it): "Allow" fixes it. The message is an emulator artifact of the dialog being dismissed, plus the Debug-only declaration.

**What I did:** nothing in the repository (no manifest line, no request in `PermissionsContext.tsx`): the documentation says nothing is required for target 36, the message has another cause, and a request or a declaration is what the page says not to add. The manifest is as it was (`git status` clean for `android/`). The Debug app on the phone is rebuilt from it (arm64 only) and installed.

**For the Builder base / the owner when the target becomes 37:** then the declaration `<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK" />` in `android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` and a runtime request (`PermissionsAndroid.request('android.permission.ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK')`, asked only when a LAN search or a LAN print starts, with an explanation through `t()`) become mandatory, and the Star library already enforces the check at API 37 (above). Its README says the same ([`react-native-star-io10` README](../../../node_modules/react-native-star-io10/README.md), "For apps targeting Android 17 or later..."). The request belongs in the wizard's search step (`PrinterEdition`) and the print run, not in the frozen files. Nothing was added now because it is not required and would be wrong at target 36. No exact new manifest lines are needed today.

**iOS (read only, `ios/` untouched).** `Info.plist` has `NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription` and `NSAllowsLocalNetworking`, no `NSBonjourServices`. The Star README (`node_modules/react-native-star-io10/README.md`, table "Some settings and approvals are required depending on the printer interface"): Ethernet needs only `NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription` (present); Bluetooth needs the Bluetooth usage description (present, `NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription`) and the external accessory protocol `jp.star-m.starpro` (+ MFi) for classic Bluetooth and USB, which `Info.plist` was not checked for here (not part of this question). The Epson library README has no iOS plist instructions; its bundled `libepos2.a` has `EpsonIoTcpFindStart` / `net_udp.h` (its own UDP broadcast discovery) and no `NSNetServiceBrowser`, `NWBrowser` or `_...._tcp` service names, so **no `NSBonjourServices` entry is needed** for either library's LAN discovery. Not seen on a device (no real printer, no iOS run by me).

## 3. Class C in the printer screens: fixed and seen

- **"Remove printer" wraps to two lines in the confirmation dialog.** Cause: the shared dialog (`shared/ConfirmDialogHost.tsx`) puts Cancel and the accept button in one row of two `flex: 1` buttons inside a box of at most the `sm` modal width, so a 14-character label has about 120 dp: **the cause is the dialog's narrow button width plus a long label; not edited (`shared/`)**. Fix in my folder: the accept button says the one word "Remove" (existing key `REMOVE`, same as `ProfilePhotoSheet`), the title stays "Remove printer" (existing key `REMOVE_PRINTER`, English unchanged). `PrinterSettings/index.tsx`, test updated. Seen: `16-remove-dialog.png` (Cancel / Remove on one line each). Not mine (proposal): other long accept labels in the app hit the same width; the dialog could stack the buttons when a label does not fit.
- **On the card "· 80 mm" starts a wrapped line.** Fix: `keepSummaryTogether` in `PrinterCard.tsx` binds each separator dot to the word before it and the width to its unit with no-break spaces (the way `62ef865` did for the Stores card), so the line breaks after a dot. New test. Seen: `11-printer-card.png` ("Generic ESC/POS ·" then "Bluetooth · 80 mm"; no line starts with a dot).

## 4. Known and left (written correctly)

A LAN search asks for the Bluetooth permission **before** the local network one: Star, the frozen `usePrinterCommands.tsx` `discoveryPrinterPort` (`interfaceType == Bluetooth || settings.autoSwitchInterface == true`, the library defaults `autoSwitchInterface` to `true`), the same in the print path; Epson, the library's own `requestAndroidPermissions()` in `PrintersDiscovery.start` for every port type. **Research on item 2 changes nothing here**: the Bluetooth gate is separate from the local network one (seen again: without Bluetooth the Star LAN search asks "Bluetooth permission is required to find printers", with it granted the next failure was the Debug local network one, section 2). Proposals of round 5 stand (ask Bluetooth only for a Bluetooth search; patch the Epson library for TCP). Not changed.

## 6. The wizard's IP address field keyboard (coordinator's item, IOS3-C1): fixed and seen on Android, iOS not seen by me

**Cause.** `PrinterFound.tsx` passed `keyboardType={... 'numbers-and-punctuation' ...}` to `OInput`, but `OInput` (`shared/OInput.tsx`, not edited) reads the keyboard from its `type` prop (`keyboardType={(props.type || 'default')}`) and never forwards `keyboardType`: the prop was ignored on both platforms and the full letters keyboard opened. Not mine (report): `OInput` ignores `keyboardType` (the only other user, `OOtpInput`, uses `TextInput` directly).

**Fix.** The address field passes `type={addressKeyboard(connection)}`: for a LAN address `numbers-and-punctuation` on iOS and `decimal-pad` on Android (the digits and the separator on the first layout; React Native 0.88 has no `numbers-and-punctuation` on Android, it falls back to text), for a Bluetooth address (letters and colons) `default`. `autoCapitalize='none'` and `autoCorrect={false}` were already passed and are forwarded by `OInput`. Because some locales' decimal pads type a comma, the handler turns every comma of a LAN address into a dot before it reaches the state (the field stays uncontrolled, as IOS-C16 made it: an address typed fast is kept whole; the value the wizard validates and saves is the normalized one). `PrinterEdition/PrinterFound.tsx`, `.../__tests__/PrinterEdition.test.tsx`: 28 tests (new: iOS and Android keyboard type, no capitals / autocorrect on both, a comma read as a dot and valid, Bluetooth keeps `default`).

**Seen on `emulator-5556`:** `30-ip-keyboard.png`: Gboard number pad with 0 to 9, a `.` key and a `,` key under the field "IP address"; `31-ip-typed.png`: "192.168.1.40" typed with real taps on the pad (dots and commas), kept whole, no "Invalid IP address". The emulator's locale is English: a comma locale was not tried. **iOS was not seen by me** (the layout name is the documented React Native value; a real iPhone was not driven in this round).
